The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-4}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of two parts: the line segment for $x\in [-4,0)$ and the line segment for $x\in [0,2].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,0).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4\cdot 4) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2].$ The corresponding region is a square, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={s}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =8+4 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
